prompt: Triangle $ABC$ is similar to triangle $DEF$. Side $AB = 6$ corresponds to side $DE = 15$, and side $BC = 8$. What is the length of side $EF$?
hint: Find the scale factor from the pair of sides you know.

hints.text: Find the scale factor from the pair of sides you know.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try an easy scale: if $AB = 2$ matches $DE = 6$, the factor is $3$, so a side of $5$ becomes $15$. Find the factor from the known pair, then apply it.

learningObjective: Use a similarity scale factor to find a missing side.
explanation: Corresponding sides of similar triangles are in a constant ratio: $\dfrac{DE}{AB} = \dfrac{15}{6} = 2.5$.
Every side of $DEF$ is $2.5$ times its partner in $ABC$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Set up a proportion instead
steps: Whichever route you take, keep the two triangles in a consistent order on both sides of the equation — mixing them up is how this question is usually lost.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Inverting the scale factor gives 8 × (6/15) = 3.2 — shrinking a triangle the problem says grew.
Decide direction first: DEF is the larger triangle, so its sides must come out LARGER. An answer smaller than 8 refutes itself.
